rules.tv_output.what: how a channel on air is encoded: encoder, picture, bitrates, how many channels and NVENC sessions at once

rules.tv.horizon_days.help: Every channel's schedule is planned this many days ahead; the guide (XMLTV) Plex and the apps read shows as far.

rules.tv.topup_below_days.help: A channel with less than this many days planned is extended back to the days ahead above. Checked every few minutes.
rules.tv.guide_max_padding_s.label: Filler added to the programme up to (s)
rules.tv.guide_max_padding_s.help: Filler (clips, bumpers, the slate) up to this long is shown as part of the programme before it; longer filler gets its own guide entry with the filler title below. As dizqueTV's guide.
rules.tv.guide_filler_title.label: Title of filler time
rules.tv.guide_filler_title.help: What the guide calls filler time that has its own entry. Empty: the channel's name.
rules.tv.guide_min_program_s.label: Shortest programme listed (s)
rules.tv.guide_min_program_s.help: Programmes shorter than this are not listed in the guide: they count as filler.
rules.tv.guide_image_max_age_s.label: Guide images kept for (s)
rules.tv.guide_image_max_age_s.help: How long Plex and other guide readers may keep a guide image (a channel's logo, a programme's poster) before asking for it again. 0: they ask every time.
rules.tv.live_lookup_reuse_seconds.label: Live page lookup reuse (seconds)
rules.tv.live_lookup_reuse_seconds.help: A live broadcast on a YouTube (or other) page is looked up with yt-dlp before it airs. Every channel airing the same page at the same time shares one lookup, reused this long; after a failure the next try looks again. A stream address (.m3u8 ...) needs no lookup.
rules.tv_output.encoder.label: Video encoder
rules.tv_output.encoder.help: auto: on a Mac, Apple VideoToolbox when its hardware encoder answers a test encode; elsewhere the NVIDIA GPU (NVENC) when it does; else the processor (libx264). nvenc, videotoolbox or software force one.
rules.tv_output.resolution.label: Picture size
rules.tv_output.resolution.help: Every programme is scaled to this (width x height); black bars keep its shape.
rules.tv_output.fps.label: Frames per second
rules.tv_output.video_kbps.label: Video bitrate (kbit/s)
rules.tv_output.audio_codec.label: Audio codec
rules.tv_output.audio_codec.help: aac plays everywhere; ac3 for players that want Dolby Digital.
rules.tv_output.audio_kbps.label: Audio bitrate (kbit/s)
rules.tv_output.segment_seconds.label: HLS segment (seconds)
rules.tv_output.segment_seconds.help: Shorter starts a channel sooner; longer is steadier on a slow network.
rules.tv_output.keyint_seconds.label: Keyframe every (seconds)
rules.tv_output.keyint_seconds.help: On the wall clock, the same in every TV process and machine, so the switch from one to another (a failover, a change going live) is seamless. Lowered to a divisor of the HLS segment.
rules.tv_output.max_active_channels.help: On each streaming host. Viewers of the same channel share its one encode; a channel nobody watches makes way for a new one. 0: 16 with VideoToolbox (Apple Silicon has several media engines), else 8.
rules.tv_output.warm_grace_seconds.label: Keep on air after the last viewer (seconds)
rules.tv_output.nvenc_max_sessions.label: Most NVENC sessions
rules.tv_output.nvenc_max_sessions.help: A GeForce card encodes only a few streams at once. Past this many a block is encoded by the processor (libx264); the channel goes back to the GPU at its next programme once a session is free. The next programme starts 3 seconds early, so a channel holds two sessions for a moment.
rules.tv_output.videotoolbox_max_session: Apple VideoToolbox sessions at once on a Mac; past this many a block is encoded by the processor (libx264) and the channel goes back at its next programme. 0: no limit.
rules.tv_output.unreadable_file_fill.lab: Instead of a file that cannot be read
rules.tv_output.unreadable_file_fill.hel: A programme whose file is missing, refused or too slow to answer. filler: the channel's filler scheduled nearest it airs in turn until the programme's end, so the next programme still starts on time. slate: the loading picture for that time.
rules.tv_output.source_timeout_seconds.h: How long a file on the share may take to be found and read before it counts as unreadable. A slow share then holds up only this channel, and only this long.
rules.tv_output.source_stall_seconds.hel: A programme whose picture stops this long (a share that hangs mid-read) is ended and the rest of its time is filled as above; its encoder session is freed for the other channels. 0: never.
The file is read again by the Length (probe) step. A file it cannot read either is listed as broken, which Repair downloads again when it is on.

rules.tv_cluster.nodes_stream.help: Machines that joined this home may encode channels too, so more channels can be on air at once. Each machine also needs "Stream on this machine" on the Live TV page. Off: the home encodes every channel.
rules.tv_cluster.policy.label: Where channels go
rules.tv_cluster.policy.help: home_first: the home until it is full (see below), then the machine with the most room. balanced: always the machine with the most room. A channel on air is never moved to even out the load.

rules.tv_cluster.failover.label: Move channels off a machine that stops
rules.tv_cluster.failover.help: A channel being watched on a machine that stops answering continues on another one at the same point of its schedule.
rules.tv_cluster.dead_after_seconds.help: Without a heartbeat for this long a machine counts as down.
rules.tv_cluster.pins.label: Preferred machine per channel
rules.tv_cluster.pins.help: Channel (its slug) -> the machine that should encode it while it is up and has room. Set it on the channel's page.
rules.tv_remote.title: Maktaba TV away from home
rules.tv_remote.what: who may watch channels away from home through Cloudflare Stream, how many at once, the monthly budget and the storage guard
rules.tv_remote.viewers.label: Who may watch away from home
rules.tv_remote.viewers.help: all: every signed-in user; admins: administrators only; listed: the users below. Watching away from home needs Cloudflare Stream set up and switched on.
rules.tv_remote.viewer_users.label: Users allowed (listed)
rules.tv_remote.max_streams_per_user.hel: How many channels one user may watch away from home at once (each device counts).
rules.tv_remote.max_channels.label: Remote channels at once
rules.tv_remote.max_channels.help: Channels sent to Cloudflare at the same time. Each uses its bitrate of the home's upload once (about 6.5 Mbit/s at the default bitrate; 22 channels about 143 Mbit/s), whatever the number of viewers. On one 1,000-minute storage block the storage, not this number, usually limits it to two.
rules.tv_remote.allowed_countries.label: Countries
rules.tv_remote.allowed_countries.help: Two-letter country codes (SA, EG, GB ...) viewers may watch from; Cloudflare checks every request. Empty: anywhere.
rules.tv_remote.idle_timeout_minutes.lab: Keep sending after the last viewer (minutes)
rules.tv_remote.idle_timeout_minutes.hel: So a viewer who comes back finds the channel at once.
rules.tv_remote.token_ttl_minutes.label: Playback link lifetime (minutes)
rules.tv_remote.token_ttl_minutes.help: A viewer's signed link stops working after this; the app renews it while it plays. Shorter cuts off a removed user sooner.
rules.tv_remote.ingest.label: How channels are sent
rules.tv_remote.ingest.help: rtmps (works with every ffmpeg with TLS) or srt (needs ffmpeg with libsrt).
rules.tv_remote.low_latency.label: Low-latency HLS (beta)
rules.tv_remote.low_latency.help: Cloudflare's low-latency HLS for new inputs.
rules.tv_remote.max_push_hours.label: Longest broadcast (hours)
rules.tv_remote.max_push_hours.help: Past this a channel's broadcast starts again (remote viewers re-buffer once), so its recording never outgrows the storage. Lower fits more channels per storage block.
rules.tv_remote.monthly_budget_usd.label: Monthly budget (USD)
rules.tv_remote.monthly_budget_usd.help: Estimated Cloudflare spend per calendar month (UTC). At 80 % the admin is told; at 100 % see below. 0: no budget check. There is no audio-only saving: Cloudflare bills minutes watched, not bytes.

rules.cluster.copies_on_operator_postgre: Copies on a Postgres you run

Off (the default): when the home's database is a Postgres you run yourself, not the one Maktaba installs, the machines keep no copy of it. On: they do, and a machine's replication role may then make a slot with any decoding plugin that Postgres has besides pgoutput (test_decoding, wal2json and the like), which reads every table, past what is published to that machine: only the home's sweep guards against it, dropping such a slot within 5 s (its database user needs pg_signal_backend and REPLICATION for that). Remove those plugins from that Postgres first. Maktaba's own Postgres has only pgoutput and needs no such rule: there this changes nothing.

emergency.kit: Its copy of {home}'s keys is from {ago}.
emergency.copy: Its copy of the library was last updated {ago}.
emergency.reason.home_answers: {home} is answering, so switch the home from {home}'s own Machines page instead.
emergency.reason.no_copy: This machine doesn't have a copy of the library yet.
emergency.reason.copy_incomplete: This machine's copy of the library isn't complete yet: it can take over once every table is copied.
emergency.reason.copy_behind: This machine's copy was more than 10 minutes behind {home} when {home} last answered, so taking over from it would lose those changes.
emergency.reason.busy: A switch is already under way.
emergency.reason.no_supervisor: This machine doesn't run under Maktaba's own service, so it can't take over.
emergency.confirm.title: Make this machine the home?
emergency.confirm.body: Do this only if {home} is gone for good. If {home} comes back, it stops and becomes one of this machine's machines. Changes it made after this machine last heard from it are kept aside, and you can apply the ones that don't conflict. Type {home} to confirm.
emergency.confirm.label: Type {home}
emergency.started: This machine is taking over as the home. It restarts in a moment.
emergency.refused: This machine can't take over right now.
homeOffline.standby: If the home is gone for good, this machine can take over as the home.

setup.move.note.worker_not_joined: This worker has not joined a home (no node config at {path}).

setup.move.progress.firewall: Windows asks you to allow the firewall rules of the app's programs
setup.move.moved: The Maktaba {machine} ran is in the app
setup.move.movedNote: Restore the old install stops the app's server and runs the old install again, as before the move. What changed in the app stays in the app.

setup.error.adopt_firewall: The firewall rules of the app's programs could not be made, so nothing was changed. Try again goes on from there.
setup.check.note.node_config_unused: {machine} holds the node config of the home {home} ({path}), which nothing here runs: setting up fresh makes a new home and leaves that node config unused.

setup.move.nocarry.serve_flag: serve {flag} (the app runs its own server)
setup.move.nocarry.firewall_rule: the firewall rule {rule} for {program} (the app has no program of that name)

setup.move.note.node_config_elsewhere: Its node config is {path}, and the app reads {app}: the app would not be this node, and a node config is never copied (one per machine).

setup.move.progress.venv: Installing the transcription tools (the old install keeps running meanwhile)
setup.move.progress.copy: Copying its keys and files into the app
setup.move.roleService: A Windows service (it runs under the system's account)
setup.move.freshNode: {machine} runs a node of the home {home} outside the app: a fresh setup would be a second copy of that node. Move it into the app instead.
setup.move.restoreNote: Restore the old install turns its task back on and runs it, as before the move. Its folder was never changed.

setup.move.underWayNote: Go on with it, or restore the old install as it ran on {machine} before.

rules.tv.loudnorm_mode.label: Loudness filter
rules.tv.loudnorm_mode.help: speechnorm: speech levelled as it plays, nothing delayed, so a channel tunes fast (what dizqueTV does). loudnorm: EBU R128 to the target below, about 3 s of look-ahead. dynaudnorm: a gentler dynamic normaliser, also with look-ahead. Only programme and filler sound is levelled, never the slate's silence.
rules.tv.speechnorm_expansion.label: Speech boost limit
rules.tv.speechnorm_expansion.help: The speechnorm filter raises a quiet passage at most this many times (dizqueTV: 6.25).

rules.system_health.title: System health
rules.system_health.what: when the System health page calls a worker late or gone, the database slow, a dependency check stale, and how long one check may take
rules.system_health.heartbeat_late_secon: A worker or a streaming machine reports every few seconds. Silent this long, it shows as late (yellow).
rules.system_health.heartbeat_gone_secon: Silent this long, a worker or streaming machine shows as gone (red). When every worker is gone, the whole page is Down.
A worker silent this long is kept as history, not shown as a failure: a machine that was switched off for good, or a worker that restarted under a new name. A worker replaced by a newer one on the same machine is history at once.
rules.system_health.db_latency_ms.label: Database slow from (ms)
rules.system_health.db_latency_ms.help: A database round trip slower than this shows the database as slow (yellow).
rules.system_health.dependency_stale_sec: The model, each share and the free disk space are checked every minute (Queue health). A check older than this shows as stale (yellow): the workers that check them may be stopped.
rules.system_health.check_timeout_ms.hel: How long the page waits for one part to answer before it shows it as not answering. Every part is checked at the same time.
rules.system_health.cache_seconds.label: Reuse an answer for (seconds)
rules.system_health.cache_seconds.help: Answers are reused this long, so many open pages cost one round of checks.

rules.search.recent_limit.label: Recent searches kept
